# libarchive / libarchive_rar5_fuzzer

libarchive's own fuzz target `libarchive_rar5_fuzzer` ([source](source/libarchive_rar5_fuzzer.cc), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libarchive (libarchive/libarchive at 3670ecf7).

Reads the input as a RAR5 archive (+ all filters, passphrase 'password'). It returns early if archive_read_new returns NULL or archive_read_open does not return ARCHIVE_OK. While archive_read_next_header returns ARCHIVE_OK, it calls pathname(_w), size, mtime, mode and is_encrypted, then reads the data while archive_read_data returns more than 0. It drops every other result and the data read. If allocating its data buffer throws std::bad_alloc, it frees the archive and returns 0. Each call first ignores SIGPIPE, as bsdtar and bsdcpio do.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libarchive at commit 3670ecf7.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/libarchive_rar5_fuzzer.cc is libarchive 3670ecf7's contrib/oss-fuzz/libarchive_rar5_fuzzer.cc with two Theorem Labs changes. On std::bad_alloc it frees any open archive and returns 0; the original aborts. It ignores SIGPIPE, as bsdtar and bsdcpio do, so a write to a filter program that stopped reading fails with EPIPE instead of killing the run.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends. Its bound statements say only how often its builds may disagree. Its decidability statements say only that some program decides where its builds agree.
